This workspace contains three folders. care_docs, care_fe, care.

In this task, let's create an agent and skill that the agent can use to generate
documentation for the care_docs folder. The agent will be responsible for analyzing the contents of the care_docs folder and generating comprehensive documentation based on the files and their structure.

Basically I should be able to select: "Care Documentation Orchestrator" agent which will include the required skill to generate documentation. This agent should be able to spin up multiple sub-agents to run things in parallel as well if supported (example: concept, and each flows could be written in parallel by orchestrating multiple parallel sub-agents), I mean you decide what's the best fastest way to do things. Use Claude Fable 5 model for researching/understanding/analyzing things. And for sub-agents to write things to the documentation, use Claude Opus 5. I'd do that, but if you think there's a more efficient way to do things, do let me know!

When generating docs, there are couple of rules to follow.

- Care is an FHIR R5 compliant HMIS software. So when describing anything, it should be in the context of FHIR R5. Always reference/link to it's source. That's the source of truth.
- Always refer to `~/ohc.network/care` (backend) `~/ohc.network/care_fe` (frontend) for any implementation details or code references. This will ensure that the documentation is accurate and aligned with the actual codebase.
- Documentation content should always STRICTLY follow Simplified Technical English (STE) guidelines. This means using clear, concise, and unambiguous language. Avoid complex sentences and jargon. Use active voice and present tense whenever possible. ASD-STE100 standard should be followed for all documentation.
- There are two main types of documentation to generate for every module or component in the care_docs folder:
  1. **Concept**: This section should provide a high-level overview of the module or component. It should explain what the module does, key attributes, its purpose, and how it fits into the overall system. Include any relevant FHIR R5 concepts and references to the source documentation.
  2. **Flow**: This section should provide a detailed explanation of the module's workflow, including how it interacts with other components in the system. It should include step-by-step explanations of processes. Reference any relevant code in `~/ohc.network/care` and `~/ohc.network/care_fe` to illustrate implementation details. Analyse the codebase and figure out all possible flows and interactions and ask the user for any missing information or clarifications if needed. NEVER assume or guess about the implementation details. Always verify with the actual codebase and ask the user for confirmation if something is slightly unclear or ambiguous.
- Concepts and Flows are user facing documentation and not technical documentation. Hence, enums and choices such as `status`, `type`, `category`, etc. should be represented in user-readable manner, and not what is used in the codebase. For example, if a status is represented as `1` in the codebase, it should be documented as `Active` or `Inactive` based on its meaning in the context of the application. Or for example, `in_progress` should be documented as `In Progress`. Always ensure that the documentation is understandable to end-users and stakeholders who may not have technical expertise. Refer the i18n's en.json file for any user-facing strings to ensure consistency in terminology and phrasing across the documentation.
- Documentation hierarchy would be 
  - Parent (eg. Clinical, user must provide this, if not ask.)
    - Module/Component Name (eg. Patient, user must provide this, if not ask.)
      - concept.md
      - flows
        - <flow_name>.md
        - <flow_name>.md

Here is an example of a concept documentation for Clinical - Patient:
```markdown
# Clinical - Patient (this should be centered using HTML align=center)

## Definition

(This section should provide a clear and concise definition of the module or component. It should explain what the module does, its purpose, and how it fits into the overall system. Include any relevant FHIR R5 concepts and references to the source documentation.)

A **patient**(link it with FHIR R5: https://build.fhir.org/patient.html) in Care is a person who receives care through your facility or program. It is the longitudinal anchor for clinical documentation- every encounter, observation, order, and care plan links back to a patient record.

## Key Attributes 
Key attributes stored within patient includes

Components | What it captures
---|---
Name | Legal and preferred names used to identify the person across the record.
Phone Number | Mobile number with country code for communication
Emergency Contact | People to reach on the patient's behalf.
Sex | The patient's gender identity
Date of Birth/ Age | Date of birth where known, or age as on date of the registration.
Blood Group | Blood group of the patient
Patient Tag | Deployment defined labels applied to the patient for classification and identification
Address | Address of correspondence
Pincode | Postal code of the patient
State | State of the patient
District to Local Body | District to ward details of the patient
Deceased Status | Whether the patient is deceased, with date of death where recorded
Identifier | Unique ID used for patient identification within the instance

### Identifier

Patients can be identified in the instance using one or more identifiers that can be configured as per the deployments requirements.

Identifiers must be unique and can be auto generated or manually updated. 

### Status

A patient record moves through a small set of states. Registration is the entry point that creates the record; the states below describe where it sits afterwards.

Status | Description
---|---
Active | The patient record is active
Deceased | The patient record is marked as deceased

## Related
Reference: Patient (technical, link to other docs)
Flow: Create a patient (link to flow.md)
Playbook: Outpatient registration (HMIS, link to playbook)
```

```markdown
# How to Create a Patient (this should be centered using HTML align=center)

## Overview

This flow describes how to register a new [patient](link to concept of patient) in Care manually.

## Pre-requisites

(This section should list any pre-requisites or conditions that must be met before the flow can be executed. It should include any necessary permissions, roles, or configurations required to perform the flow. For example, to create an encounter, you first need a patient to be registered.)

(example:)
- The logged in user must be part of the facility
- Required permissions for creating a patient must be there

## Permissions

(Always refer the backend's RBAC implementation for permissions and authorize_* functions in relevant viewsets. Analayze the backend's codebase and specify how to look for permissions so that agents can find the required permissions easily without again having to read the entire codebase to analyze how RBAC works.)

Permission | Access
---|---
Can create patient | Allows the user to create a new patient.
Can list patient | Allows the user to view the list of patients.

## Steps

### 1. Open Patient Registration Form

From the facility dashboard, select Patients from the left navigation menu.
- Click Search Patients.
- Select Add New Patient to start a new registration.

### Enter Patient Details

Complete the patient registration form - The form is divided into two sections:
- **Patient Basics**: Enter the patient's primary demographic information, including:

Components | What it captures
---|---
Name | Legal and preferred names used to identify the person across the record.
Phone Number | Mobile number with country code for communication
Emergency Contact | People to reach on the patient's behalf.
Sex | The patient's gender identity
Date of Birth/ Age | Date of birth where known, or age as on date of the registration.
Blood Group | Blood group of the patient
Patient Tag | Deployment defined labels applied to the patient for classification and identification
- **Additional Details**: Provide any additional information required by your deployment, such as:

Components | What it captures
---|---
Address | Address of correspondence
Pincode | Postal code of the patient
State | State of the patient
District to Local Body | District to ward details of the patient
Deceased Status | Whether the patient is deceased, with date of death where recorded
Identifier | Unique ID used for patient identification within the instance

Note: Which fields are mandatory depends on your deployment’s configuration. (Always refer to care_config to know if there are configurations that affects behaviour and include it it notes or relevant steps)

### Register the Patient
- Click the Register button to submit the form.
- You could also use the keyboard shortcut `Ctrl + Enter` to submit the form. (always refer keyboard shortcuts in care_fe and include it in the steps if applicable)

### Expected Outcome
- A patient is created with the details entered.
- A patient ID is assigned according to the deployment's and facility identifier    configuration.

### Related

Concepts: 
 - Patient
 - ...

Flows: 
 - Search for a patient
```

## CARE Backend Codebase Navigation Guide

### 1. RBAC / Permissions

**Permission Definitions Structure:**
- Location: `care/security/permissions/`
- Files: Domain-specific enums (e.g., `patient.py`, `encounter.py`, `facility.py`, `questionnaire.py`, etc.) + `base.py` (aggregator), `constants.py` (Permission/PermissionContext classes)
- All 40+ domain permissions defined: [permissions directory](care/security/permissions)

**Permission Naming Convention:**
- Pattern: `can_<action>_<resource>` (e.g., `can_create_patient`, `can_write_patient`, `can_list_patients`)
- Example from [patient.py](care/security/permissions/patient.py):
  ```python
  class PatientPermissions(enum.Enum):
      can_create_patient = Permission(
          "Can Create Patient",
          "",
          PermissionContext.PATIENT,
          [STAFF_ROLE, DOCTOR_ROLE, NURSE_ROLE, ADMINISTRATOR, ADMIN_ROLE, FACILITY_ADMIN_ROLE],
      )
  ```

**Permission/PermissionContext Classes:**
- Location: [care/security/permissions/constants.py](care/security/permissions/constants.py)
- `Permission` dataclass: wraps name, description, context (PermissionContext enum), and list of roles
- `PermissionContext` enum: GENERIC, FACILITY, PATIENT, QUESTIONNAIRE, ORGANIZATION, FACILITY_ORGANIZATION, ENCOUNTER

**Viewset Authorization Pattern:**
- Base Classes: [EMRCreateMixin](care/emr/api/viewsets/base.py), [EMRRetrieveMixin](care/emr/api/viewsets/base.py), [EMRUpdateMixin](care/emr/api/viewsets/base.py), [EMRDestroyMixin](care/emr/api/viewsets/base.py) 
- Concrete Example: [PatientViewSet](care/emr/api/viewsets/patient.py#L56-L81) — implements `authorize_create()`, `authorize_update()`, `authorize_destroy()`
- Pattern: Each mixin provides override hook (e.g., `authorize_create(instance)`, `authorize_retrieve(model_instance)`, `authorize_update(request_obj, model_instance)`)
- Authorization delegates to `AuthorizationController.call("can_<action>_<resource>", user, obj)`

**Role Definition & Permission Mapping:**
- Roles Location: [care/security/roles/role.py](care/security/roles/role.py)
- Predefined Roles: VOLUNTEER_ROLE, DOCTOR_ROLE, NURSE_ROLE, STAFF_ROLE, PHARMACIST_ROLE, ADMINISTRATOR, FACILITY_ADMIN_ROLE, ADMIN_ROLE, + ROLE_ORGANIZATION_* variants
- Permission-to-Role Mapping: Model in `security/models` (RolePermission model — maps role IDs to permission slugs)

**Authorization Controller:**
- Location: [care/security/authorization/base.py](care/security/authorization/base.py)
- Core Class: `AuthorizationController` — caches and dispatches `can_*` and `get_*` methods from registered handlers
- Handler Pattern: `AuthorizationHandler` subclasses (one per domain, e.g., `PatientAccess` in [care/security/authorization/patient.py](care/security/authorization/patient.py))
- Method Dispatch: `AuthorizationController.call("can_action_name", user, obj)` → looks up handler, calls handler's method
- Concrete Example in [patient.py](care/security/authorization/patient.py): `can_create_patient(user)`, `can_write_patient_obj(user, patient)`, `can_view_patient_obj(user, patient)`
- Handler Methods use: `check_permission_in_facility_organization()`, `check_permission_in_organization()` — validate user's role+organization against permission slug

---

### 2. EMR Domain Structure

**Directory Layout:**
- Models: [care/emr/models/](care/emr/models/) — 40+ domain models (patient.py, encounter.py, questionnaire.py, etc.)
- Pydantic Resource Specs: [care/emr/resources/](care/emr/resources/) — organized in subdirectories per domain (patient/, encounter/, questionnaire/, etc.), with `spec.py` containing pydantic BaseModel classes
- Viewsets: [care/emr/api/viewsets/](care/emr/api/viewsets/) — one per domain (patient.py, encounter.py, etc.), inheriting from mixins
- API Routing: [config/api_router.py](config/api_router.py) — registers viewsets with DRF router

**FHIR Alignment:**
- ValueSet/Coding System: [care/emr/registries/](care/emr/registries/) and [care/emr/resources/*/valueset.py](care/emr/resources/encounter/valueset.py)
- Example from encounter: References SNOMED CT system (`http://snomed.info/sct`) and FHIR value sets
- Status enums reference FHIR codes: e.g., encounter StatusChoices (planned, in_progress, on_hold, discharged, completed, cancelled, etc.)

**Enum/Choices for Statuses:**
- Location: [care/emr/resources/encounter/constants.py](care/emr/resources/encounter/constants.py)
- Example: `StatusChoices(str, Enum)` with values like `planned`, `in_progress`, `on_hold`, `discharged`, `completed`, `cancelled`, `discontinued`, `entered_in_error`
- Display Mapping: [care/emr/resources/encounter/enum_display_names.py](care/emr/resources/encounter/enum_display_names.py) — functions like `get_admit_source_display(value)` return human-readable strings (e.g., "Transferred from other hospital")

**Patient Status Enums:**
- Location: [care/emr/resources/patient/spec.py](care/emr/resources/patient/spec.py)
- Examples: `BloodGroupChoices`, `GenderChoices` (male, female, non_binary, transgender)
- Deceased tracking: `deceased_datetime` field on Patient model with validation in resource spec

**EMRResource Base Class:**
- Location: [care/emr/resources/base.py](care/emr/resources/base.py)
- Pattern: Pydantic BaseModel subclass mapping Django models ↔ JSON
- Methods: `serialize(obj, user)` (model→pydantic), `de_serialize(obj=None)` (pydantic→model)
- Metadata: `__model__` points to Django model, `__exclude__` lists fields not serialized, `__store_metadata__` flag for metadata JSON field

**Questionnaire Structure:**
- Model: [care/emr/models/questionnaire.py](care/emr/models/questionnaire.py) — tracks internal_revision, slug, auth_context (instance/facility/user/facility_organization), questions JSON
- Resource Spec: [care/emr/resources/questionnaire/spec.py](care/emr/resources/questionnaire/spec.py) — defines QuestionType enum (group, boolean, string, choice, quantity, etc.), EnableOperator, AnswerConstraint
- Viewsets: [care/emr/api/viewsets/questionnaire/](care/emr/api/viewsets/questionnaire/) — questionnaire.py (CRUD), questionnaire_response.py (responses), resource_questionnaire_response.py
- Utilities: [care/emr/resources/questionnaire/utils.py](care/emr/resources/questionnaire/utils.py)

---

### 3. Configuration Affecting Behavior

**Settings Files:**
- Base Config: [config/settings/base.py](config/settings/base.py) — Django settings, caches, middleware, auth
- Environment-Specific: [config/settings/](config/settings/) — local.py, deployment.py, staging.py, test.py, production.py
- Application Config: [config/settings/config.py](config/settings/config.py) — business logic settings (feature toggles, limits)

**Feature Flags & Feature-Affecting Settings:**
- `PATIENT_GLOBAL_EDIT_ACCESS_ENABLED` (env var) — allows editing patient globally if false requires role association
  - Grep pattern: `PATIENT_GLOBAL_EDIT_ACCESS_ENABLED`
  - Used in: [care/emr/api/viewsets/patient.py#L100](care/emr/api/viewsets/patient.py#L100), [care/security/authorization/patient.py#L61](care/security/authorization/patient.py#L61)
  
**Patient Identifier Configuration:**
- Config Flags (strings in `.env`): `MAINTAIN_PATIENT_NAME_IDENTIFIER`, `MAINTAIN_PATIENT_PHONE_NUMBER_IDENTIFIER`, `MAINTAIN_FACILITY_PATIENT_NAME_IDENTIFIER`, `PATIENT_NAME_MAX_LENGTH`
  - Location: [config/settings/config.py](config/settings/config.py) (lines 260–280)
- Model: `PatientIdentifierConfig` model in [care/emr/models/patient.py](care/emr/models/patient.py)
- Resource: [care/emr/resources/patient/spec.py](care/emr/resources/patient/spec.py) — `PatientIdentifierConfigRequest` spec
- Authorization: [care/security/authorization/patient_identifier_config.py](care/security/authorization/patient_identifier_config.py) — `can_list_facility_patient_identifier_config`, `can_write_facility_patient_identifier_config`

**Other Business Config Settings:**
- Max limits: `MAX_DATAPOINTS_PER_UPSERT`, `MAX_REQUESTS_PER_BATCH_REQUEST`, `MAX_APPOINTMENTS_PER_PATIENT`, `MAX_ACTIVE_ENCOUNTERS_PER_PATIENT_IN_FACILITY`
- Encounter Config: `ENCOUNTER_RESTART_TIME_LIMIT_HOURS`, `INVOICE_FREE_CANCEL_PERIOD_MINUTES`, `CHARGE_ITEM_FREE_CANCEL_PERIOD_MINUTES`
- Tax/Discount Codes: `TAX_CODES`, `DISCOUNT_CODES`, `TAX_MONETARY_COMPONENT_DEFINITIONS`, `DISCOUNT_MONETARY_COMPONENT_DEFINITIONS`

**Plugin System:**
- Config: [plug_config.py](plug_config.py) — PlugManager instantiation
- Registrations: Permitting domain handlers to register via `@classmethod register_internal_controller(cls, controller)` in [care/security/authorization/base.py](care/security/authorization/base.py)

---

### 4. Questionnaires

**Models:**
- [care/emr/models/questionnaire.py](care/emr/models/questionnaire.py) — Questionnaire model with fields: `internal_revision`, `slug`, `auth_context`, `questions` (JSON), `subject_type`, `status`
- Related: `QuestionnaireFacilityOrganization`, `QuestionnaireResponse` (in care/emr/models/)

**Resource Specs:**
- [care/emr/resources/questionnaire/spec.py](care/emr/resources/questionnaire/spec.py) — enums for QuestionType, EnableOperator, DisabledDisplay, AnswerConstraint
- Questionnaire response specs in `questionnaire_response/spec.py`

**Viewsets:**
- [care/emr/api/viewsets/questionnaire/](care/emr/api/viewsets/questionnaire/) directory:
  - `questionnaire.py` — QuestionnaireViewSet (CRUD)
  - `questionnaire_response.py` — QuestionnaireResponseViewSet
  - `resource_questionnaire_response.py` — detailed response handling
  - `resource_authz.py` — authorization for questionnaire responses
  - `resource_observation.py` — observation-type questionnaire responses

**Authorization:**
- [care/security/authorization/questionnaire.py](care/security/authorization/questionnaire.py) — QuestionnaireAccess handler
- [care/security/permissions/questionnaire.py](care/security/permissions/questionnaire.py) — QuestionnairePermissions enum

---

### 5. Tests & Fixtures

**Fixture System:**
- Documentation: [care/fixtures/fixtures.md](care/fixtures/fixtures.md) — comprehensive guide
- Base Helper: [care/fixtures/base.py](care/fixtures/base.py) — `CareFixtureBase` class wraps APIClient, provides `create_*` methods for resources
- Constants: [care/fixtures/constants.py](care/fixtures/constants.py) — reusable data (medical codes, arrays, builders)
- Fixture Scripts: [care/fixtures/scripts/](care/fixtures/scripts/) — default_fixtures.py (seed data), questionnaire_e2e_fixtures.py (E2E test data)

**Load Fixtures Command:**
- Command: `python manage.py load_fixtures` (or `make load-fixtures`)
- Usage: `python manage.py load_fixtures --path care/fixtures/scripts/custom.py`
- Requires: `DEBUG=True`
- Mechanism: Runs Python file via `runpy.run_path()` with `care_fixture_context()` manager

**Fixture Context:**
- Location: [care/fixtures/context.py](care/fixtures/context.py)
- Usage: `with care_fixture_context() as base:` provides authenticated APIClient

**What load_fixtures Does:**
- Seeds database via REST API (all validations, signals, audit logs run)
- Creates organizations, facilities, patients, encounters, questionnaires, users, roles
- Example: [default_fixtures.py](care/fixtures/scripts/default_fixtures.py) orchestrates full setup
- E2E questionnaires: `questionnaire_e2e_fixtures.py` creates deterministic set with `e2e-` prefix slugs

---

## Goal
Create a multi-agent documentation pipeline in `care_docs/.github/` that generates user-facing Concept + Flow docs for CARE modules, grounded in FHIR R5, the care backend, and care_fe frontend, following ASD-STE100.

### Recommended model map

Role | Plan model | Better model | Reason
Orchestrator | Fable 5 | Sonnet 5 | It coordinates and merges. It does not need the top tier.
Researcher | Fable 5 | Sonnet 5 | It reads code and builds a dossier. Sonnet 5 is enough.
Writer | "Opus 5" | Opus 5 | It writes the docs. The text quality matters.

Fable 5 has safety classifiers. The classifiers route cybersecurity, biology, chemistry, and distillation prompts to an Opus 4.8 fallback, and you pay Fable 5 rates for that Opus 4.8 output. Your researchers read RBAC, permission, and auth code. This code can trigger the cybersecurity classifier. So Fable 5 can give you Opus 4.8 work at a higher price. [Tygart Media](https://tygartmedia.com/claude-models-comparison/)

Fable 5 is also slow. Complex tasks take 60 seconds to several minutes, against 3 to 15 seconds for Opus 4.8. Your researchers run in parallel and run often. This delay adds up. [Tygart Media](https://tygartmedia.com/claude-models-comparison/)

- Each member is a `Permission` dataclass: display name, description, `PermissionContext`

  ENCOUNTER), and the list of roles that hold it. **The first argument is the

1. Open the domain viewset: `care/emr/api/viewsets/{domain}.py`

{"content": "# Simplified Technical English (ASD-STE100) Rules

All documentation content MUST follow these rules. The reviewer rejects text that
breaks them.

## Sentence rules

- Maximum 20 words per sentence in procedures (Steps sections).
- Maximum 25 words per sentence in descriptions (Definition, Overview sections).
- One instruction per sentence. Do not chain actions with "and then".
- One topic per paragraph. Maximum 6 sentences per paragraph.

## Voice and tense

- Use active voice. Write "The system creates a patient record", not
  "A patient record is created by the system".
- Use present tense. Write "Care assigns an ID", not "Care will assign an ID".
- Use the command form (imperative) for instructions: "Click Save.", "Select Patients."

## Words

name: care-docs-generation

# CARE Documentation Generation

Pipeline for generating user-facing Concept and Flow documentation for CARE modules,
orchestrated by the **Care Documentation Orchestrator** agent with parallel subagents.

## Output structure

```
care_docs/
  <Parent>/                 # e.g., Clinical — ask the user if missing
    <Module>/               # e.g., Patient — ask the user if missing
      concept.md
      flows/
        <flow_name>.md      # snake_case, one file per flow
```

## Roles

| Agent | Model tier | Job |
|---|---|---|
| care-docs-orchestrator | Sonnet | Coordinate; never writes docs |
| care-docs-researcher | Sonnet | Read-only codebase research → dossier |
| care-docs-writer | Opus | Write exactly one doc per invocation |
| care-docs-reviewer | Opus | One module-wide compliance pass, edits in place |

## Procedure

1. **Inputs.** Require `Parent` and `Module` from the user. If missing, ask.
   Optionally accept a list of flows to document.
2. **Research (parallel).** Spawn TWO `care-docs-researcher` subagents in the SAME
   batch — one focused on the backend (`~/ohc.network/care`), one on the frontend
   (`~/ohc.network/care_fe`). Both use
   [codebase-navigation.md](./references/codebase-navigation.md) and return a
   structured dossier.
3. **Merge and confirm.** Merge the dossiers. Present to the user:
   the proposed flow list, key attributes, statuses with display labels, and ALL
   ambiguities the researchers flagged. **Wait for user confirmation of the flow
   list before writing. Never guess unresolved details.**
4. **Write (parallel).** Spawn ONE `care-docs-writer` subagent per document
   (1 concept + N flows) in a SINGLE parallel batch. Give each writer:
   - the exact output file path,
   - the doc type (concept | flow),
   - the relevant dossier excerpt (verified facts only),
   - the sibling doc list for cross-links (Related sections).
5. **Review.** Spawn ONE `care-docs-reviewer` subagent over
   `care_docs/<Parent>/<Module>/`. It edits files in place and returns a change
   summary plus unresolved issues.
6. **Report.** Summarize created files, reviewer changes, and open questions.

## Rules (all agents)

- [doc-rules.md](./references/doc-rules.md) — FHIR R5 grounding, user-readable
  enums, hierarchy, cross-linking, never-guess policy.
- [ste-rules.md](./references/ste-rules.md) — ASD-STE100 language rules.
- [codebase-navigation.md](./references/codebase-navigation.md) — pre-verified
  paths and grep patterns for both repos. Use it; do not re-derive it.

## Templates

- Concept: [concept-template.md](./assets/concept-template.md)
- Flow: [flow-template.md](./assets/flow-template.md)

Docs pages 404'd; I'll go on the local VS Code reference, which documents `tools` as per-agent frontmatter and `handoffs` only as "transitions to other agents".

**The root cause:** your orchestrator has `tools: [read, search, agent, todo]` — deliberately no `edit`/`execute`, so it can't touch code. But subagents declare their **own** tools; the parent only needs `agent` to invoke them. So the fix is a fixer subagent, not loosening the orchestrator.

**Options**

| Option | How | Trade-off |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Dedicated `care-code-fixer` subagent** ✅ | Hidden agent with `[read, search, edit, execute]`, added to the orchestrator's `agents:` allowlist | Fix happens in-session, in parallel; orchestrator stays read-only. Best fit |
| B. `handoffs:` frontmatter | Transition the session to a coding agent | Switches the *whole* session; you lose the docs run in progress |
| C. Drop the `agents:` allowlist | Omit the field → any agent invocable | Works, but imprecise; orchestrator could pull in unrelated agents |
| D. Give the orchestrator `edit`/`execute` | One-line change | Rejected — the docs pipeline could then silently rewrite app code |

Implementing A:

Yes — and better than I expected. Playwright 1.60 (which care_fe has) supports **video annotations**: `show.actions` outlines each clicked element with a caption, and `show.test` burns in the current `test.step()` name. That solves the two classic problems with automated demo videos — an invisible mouse cursor and no narration.

**The mechanism**

1. Add a `docs` project to [playwright.config.ts](care_fe/playwright.config.ts) — separate from the `chromium` test project so real E2E runs stay fast:

```ts
{
  name: "docs",
  testDir: "./tests/docs",
  testMatch: /.*\.demo\.ts/,
  dependencies: ["setup"],
  use: {
    ...devices["Desktop Chrome"],
    viewport: { width: 1280, height: 720 },
    video: {
      mode: "on",
      size: { width: 1280, height: 720 },
      show: {
        actions: { duration: 800, position: "top-right" },  // highlights the clicked element
        test: { level: "step", position: "top-left" },      // burns in test.step() titles
      },
    },
    launchOptions: { slowMo: 400 },  // human-watchable pacing
  },
}
```

2. Write one `.demo.ts` per flow where each `test.step()` title **is** the flow doc's step heading — the captions and the markdown then stay in sync by construction.
3. Save to a stable filename with `page.video().saveAs(...)` in an `afterEach` (Playwright's default names are hashes).
4. Embed in the flow doc.

Everything else is already in place: `tests/.auth/*.json` storage state, the DB snapshot restore in `globalSetup`, and `tests/support/*Id.ts` fixture IDs — so recordings are deterministic and repeatable.

**The real constraints**

- **Format**: Playwright emits WebM only. MP4 or GIF needs ffmpeg, which isn't installed and isn't referenced anywhere in care_fe.
- **Embedding**: care_docs has no static-site generator and no git remote, so I can't tell where these render. This matters — a repo-relative `<video>` tag behaves differently on github.com versus a docs site, and I'd want to verify rather than guess.
- **Size/storage**: 10 encounter flows × a few hundred KB is fine in git; a full module set may want Git LFS.
- `.markdownlint.json` currently allows only `<h1>` inline HTML — `video` would need adding.

2. `playwright.config.ts` with a single `docs` project (see config below).
3. `.gitignore` entries for `node_modules/`, `test-results/`, and the raw

4. `ffmpeg` installed (`brew install ffmpeg`). It is NOT currently installed and is

Ask the user before creating this bootstrap. Do not add it silently.

## Prerequisites for every recording run

Recordings drive the real application, so the full local stack must be up:

1. **Backend** running on port 9000 (see `care/CLAUDE.md`).
2. **Frontend production build** served at `http://localhost:4000`
   (`npm run build && npm run preview` in `care_fe`).
3. **Clean database** — in `care_fe`, run `npm run playwright:db-restore`.

4. **Fresh auth state** — in `care_fe`, run `npx playwright test --project=setup`.

   `care_fe/tests/support/`. Tokens rotate, so refresh them before a recording

## Recording config

```ts
// care_docs/playwright.config.ts
use: {
  ...devices["Desktop Chrome"],
  baseURL: "http://localhost:4000",
  storageState: "../care_fe/tests/.auth/user.json",
  viewport: { width: 1280, height: 720 },
  video: {
    mode: "on",
    size: { width: 1280, height: 720 },
    show: {
      actions: { duration: 800, position: "top-right", fontSize: 14 },
      test: { level: "step", position: "top-left", fontSize: 14 },
    },
  },
  launchOptions: { slowMo: 400 },
}
```

Why these settings:

- `show.actions` outlines each target element and captions the action. Playwright
  videos do NOT show a mouse cursor, so this is what makes the video followable.
- `show.test` with `level: "step"` burns the current `test.step()` title into the
  frame. This is the narration.
- `slowMo` gives human-watchable pacing. Without it the flow is a blur.
- Video size defaults to the viewport scaled to fit 800x800, so set both.

## Writing a demo spec

One spec per flow doc, named to match the doc:
`care_docs/recordings/<Parent>/<Module>/<index>. <Flow name>.demo.ts`

Rules:

- **Each `test.step()` title MUST equal the matching step heading in the flow doc.**
  The burned-in caption and the written doc then stay in sync by construction.
- Use the same locator style as `care_fe/tests/` (`getByRole`, `getByLabel`) and the
  helpers in `care_fe/tests/helper/ui.ts`.
- Use fixture IDs from `care_fe/tests/support/*Id.ts` instead of hardcoded IDs.
- Generate unique data with `faker` so re-runs do not collide.
- Add a short settle pause at the end so the final state is visible.
- Save the video to a stable name — Playwright's default filenames are hashes:

  ```ts
  await page.close(); // finalizes the video
  await page.video()?.saveAs(rawWebmPath);
  ```

- Do NOT assert like a test. A recording that fails mid-way produces a useless video.
  Keep assertions to the minimum needed to wait for the UI to settle.

## Converting to MP4

Playwright emits WebM only. Convert each recording:

```sh
ffmpeg -y -i "<raw>.webm" \
  -c:v libx264 -profile:v high -pix_fmt yuv420p \
  -crf 26 -preset slow -movflags +faststart -an \
  "<Parent>/<Module>/media/<index>. <Flow name>.mp4"
```

- `-pix_fmt yuv420p` is required, or Safari and QuickTime will not play the file.
- `-movflags +faststart` lets playback begin before the whole file downloads.
- `-an` drops the (empty) audio track.
- `-crf 26` is a reasonable size/quality trade-off. Lower means larger and sharper.

Optional poster frame:

```sh
ffmpeg -y -i "<file>.mp4" -vframes 1 "<file>.png"
```

## Embedding in the flow doc

Add the video directly under the `## Overview` section:

```html
<video src="https://github.com/<org>/care_docs/raw/<branch>/<path>.mp4" controls></video>
```

**Verify this renders before generating a full batch.** GitHub documents `.mp4`
support for files *attached to* issues, pull requests, and discussions. It does not
document whether a `<video>` tag inside a committed markdown file plays on
github.com, and relative `src` paths are unlikely to work. Test one file first.

Fallback that always works — a poster image linking to the video:

```markdown
[![Watch the demo](./media/<file>.png)](./media/<file>.mp4)
```

Note: `.markdownlint.json` must list `video` under `MD033.allowed_elements` for the
HTML form to lint clean.

## Size and storage

- Keep each recording under roughly 30 seconds. Long flows should be split.
- Expect a few hundred KB to ~2 MB per flow at these settings.
- Commit the MP4s; do NOT commit the raw `.webm` intermediates.
- If a module's media folder grows past tens of megabytes, move to Git LFS.

## Gotchas

- The video is only written when the page or browser context closes.
- Videos capture the viewport only, never real browser chrome or OS windows.
- Any patient or user data on screen is baked into the video. Use fixture data only.
  Never record against a database with real patient information.
- Re-run `playwright:db-restore` between takes, or repeat runs drift as data accumulates.

   (`npm run build && npm run preview` in `care_fe`).
3. **Clean database** — in `care_fe`, run `npm run playwright:db-restore`.
   First time: `npm run playwright:db-reset` with `CARE_BACKEND_DIR` set.
4. **Fresh auth state** — in `care_fe`, run `npx playwright test --project=setup`.
   This writes `care_fe/tests/.auth/*.json` and the fixture IDs in
   `care_fe/tests/support/`. Tokens rotate, so refresh them before a recording
   session. The `care_docs` config reads these files by relative path.

## Recording config

```ts
// care_docs/playwright.config.ts
use: {
  ...devices["Desktop Chrome"],
  baseURL: "http://localhost:4000",
  storageState: "../care_fe/tests/.auth/user.json",
  viewport: { width: 1280, height: 720 },
  video: {
    mode: "on",
    size: { width: 1280, height: 720 },
    show: {
      actions: { duration: 800, position: "top-right", fontSize: 14 },
      test: { level: "step", position: "top-left", fontSize: 14 },
    },
  },
  launchOptions: { slowMo: 400 },
}
```

Why these settings:

- `show.actions` outlines each target element and captions the action. Playwright
  videos do NOT show a mouse cursor, so this is what makes the video followable.
- `show.test` with `level: "step"` burns the current `test.step()` title into the
  frame. This is the narration.
- `slowMo` gives human-watchable pacing. Without it the flow is a blur.
- Video size defaults to the viewport scaled to fit 800x800, so set both.

## Writing a demo spec

One spec per flow doc, named to match the doc:
`care_docs/recordings/<Parent>/<Module>/<index>. <Flow name>.demo.ts`

Rules:

- **Each `test.step()` title MUST equal the matching step heading in the flow doc.**
  The burned-in caption and the written doc then stay in sync by construction.
- Use the same locator style as `care_fe/tests/` (`getByRole`, `getByLabel`) and the
  helpers in `care_fe/tests/helper/ui.ts`.
- Use fixture IDs from `care_fe/tests/support/*Id.ts` instead of hardcoded IDs.
- Generate unique data with `faker` so re-runs do not collide.
- Add a short settle pause at the end so the final state stays on screen.
- Save the video to a stable name — Playwright's default filenames are hashes:

  ```ts
  await page.close(); // finalizes the video
  await page.video()?.saveAs(rawWebmPath);
  ```

- Do NOT assert like a test. A recording that fails mid-way produces a useless video.
  Keep assertions to the minimum needed to wait for the UI to settle.

## Converting to MP4

Playwright emits WebM only. Convert each recording:

```sh
ffmpeg -y -i "<raw>.webm" \
  -c:v libx264 -profile:v high -pix_fmt yuv420p \
  -crf 26 -preset slow -movflags +faststart -an \
  "<Parent>/<Module>/media/<index>. <Flow name>.mp4"
```

- `-pix_fmt yuv420p` is required, or Safari and QuickTime will not play the file.
- `-movflags +faststart` lets playback begin before the whole file downloads.
- `-an` drops the (empty) audio track.
- `-crf 26` is a reasonable size/quality trade-off. Lower means larger and sharper.

Poster frame (needed for the fallback embed):

```sh
ffmpeg -y -i "<file>.mp4" -vframes 1 "<file>.png"
```

## Embedding in the flow doc

Add the video directly under the `## Overview` section:

```html
<video src="https://github.com/<org>/care_docs/raw/<branch>/<path>.mp4" controls></video>
```

**Verify this renders before you generate a full batch.** GitHub documents `.mp4`
support for files *attached to* issues, pull requests, and discussions. It does not
document whether a `<video>` tag inside a committed markdown file plays on
github.com, and relative `src` paths are unlikely to work. Test one file first.

Fallback that always works — a poster image linking to the video:

```markdown
[![Watch the demo](../media/<file>.png)](../media/<file>.mp4)
```

`.markdownlint.json` lists `video` under `MD033.allowed_elements`, so the HTML form
lints clean.

## Size and storage

- Keep each recording under roughly 30 seconds. Split long flows.
- Expect a few hundred KB to about 2 MB per flow at these settings.
- Commit the MP4 and poster files. Do NOT commit the raw `.webm` intermediates.
- If a module's media folder grows past tens of megabytes, move to Git LFS.

## Gotchas

- The video is only written when the page or browser context closes.
- Videos capture the viewport only, never real browser chrome or OS windows.
- Everything on screen is baked into the video permanently. Use fixture data only.
  NEVER record against a database that holds real patient information.
- Run `playwright:db-restore` between takes, or repeat runs drift as data accumulates.

content.name: run_in_terminal

content.text:
Diagnosed. The chain is clear from the log:

```
⚠️ No DB snapshot found. Run 'npm run playwright:db-reset' to create one.
⚠️ Token refresh failed with status: 401
```

1. **No DB snapshot exists**, so `globalSetup` never restored anything — your DB was left as-is.
2. Admin login then failed: after submitting credentials, the `Hey <name>` heading never appears. Nurse login *passed*, so the backend and auth work — the `admin`/`admin` fixture user just isn't in this database.
3. Everything downstream failed on expired tokens because `auth.setup.ts` never wrote a fresh `user.json`.

So the DB has never been seeded with the fixture data these tests assume. The documented fix is the full reset — which is the more destructive option you didn't pick earlier, so I'm asking rather than assuming.

Important finding — the reset didn't do what it looks like:

```
NOTICE: database "care" does not exist, skipping
```

`playwright-db.sh` dropped/created a database named **`care`**, but your running backend is connected to a *different* database. The fixture loader seeds via the REST API, so it hit your real DB — which already had a "Kerala" organization. Nothing was actually reset.

That also reframes the earlier failure: your DB likely already has fixture data, and `admin` login may be failing on the UI assertion rather than on auth. Let me verify directly against the API.

content.text:
Researched the current docs. Short answer: this becomes a **Claude Code plugin** distributed via a **marketplace git repo** — and Claude Desktop users reach it through Claude Code/Cowork inside Desktop (paid plans). There's no separate "Desktop plugin" format for agents/skills; Desktop *Extensions* are MCP servers, which is a different thing.

## The target structure

```
care-docs-plugin/
├── .claude-plugin/plugin.json     # name, description, version, author
├── agents/                        # the 5 agents
├── skills/care-docs-generation/   # SKILL.md + references/ + assets/
└── hooks/hooks.json               # optional: enforce the localhost guard
```

Published from a marketplace repo with `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`; users run `/plugin marketplace add ohcnetwork/claude-plugins` then `/plugin install care-docs@ohcnetwork`. Local testing is `claude --plugin-dir ./care-docs-plugin`.

## What actually needs doing

| # | Work | Effort | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Restructure into plugin layout | Small | Mostly moving files. `.github/skills/…` → `skills/…`, `.github/agents/` → `agents/` |
| 2 | **Rewrite all frontmatter** | Medium | Biggest mechanical change — see below |
| 3 | **De-hardcode the environment** | **Large** | The real blocker |
| 4 | Decide the recording story | Medium | The Playwright bootstrap can't ship as-is |
| 5 | Marketplace repo + `claude plugin validate` | Small | Optional community submission after |

**On #2 — the frontmatter is Copilot-specific and none of it survives as-is:**
- `model: ["Claude Sonnet 5 (copilot)", …]` → `sonnet` / `opus` / `inherit`
- `tools: [read, search, edit, execute, agent, todo]` → Claude Code tool names (`Read`, `Edit`, `Bash`, `Grep`, `Glob`, `Task`, …)
- `user-invocable`, `disable-model-invocation`, `argument-hint` — VS Code concepts
- **`agents: [...]` allowlist has no Claude Code equivalent.** Subagent selection there is description-driven. Our orchestrator's careful "only these five subagents" constraint becomes advisory prose rather than enforced config — worth knowing before you rely on it.

**On #3 — this is what makes it more than a weekend job.** The pipeline currently assumes:
- repos at `~/ohc.network/care` and `~/ohc.network/care_fe`
- backend on `:9000`, frontend on `:4000`
- `care_docs` as the output root

All hardcoded, in [codebase-navigation.md](../care_docs/.github/skills/care-docs-generation/references/codebase-navigation.md), [flow-recording.md](../care_docs/.github/skills/care-docs-generation/references/flow-recording.md), and [care.ts](../care_docs/recordings/support/care.ts). And plugins are **copied to a cache dir on install**, so nothing can reference paths outside the plugin directory. You'd need env vars (`CARE_BACKEND_DIR`, `CARE_FE_DIR`, `CARE_DOCS_DIR`) plus a first-run setup skill that detects or asks for them.

**On #4** — the recording half depends on Playwright, ffmpeg, Postgres, a seeded DB, and care_fe's auth fixtures. I'd ship v1 **docs-only** (researcher/writer/reviewer) and keep recording as a documented opt-in that the user bootstraps in their own repo. Trying to make recording work on a fresh install is where this balloons.

## Two things worth deciding first

1. **Who's the audience?** The navigation guide is deeply CARE-specific — permission traces, `{PREFIX}__{value}` i18n keys, encounter specs. This is a plugin *for CARE contributors*, not a general docs plugin. That argues for a public `ohcnetwork/claude-plugins` marketplace rather than community-marketplace submission.
2. **Do you want VS Code and Claude Code to stay in sync?** Two copies of five agents will drift. Options: make the plugin canonical and generate the VS Code variants, or accept the fork. Worth choosing now rather than after divergence.

**My recommendation:** scope v1 as docs-only, env-var-configured, in a public marketplace repo — that's maybe a day's work and genuinely installable. Recording stays a documented extension.

File creation and terminal are both disabled now, so I can't build it. Here's the design I'd landed on, ready to execute when you re-enable them.

## Key decision: invert the source of truth

Rather than maintaining two copies, keep **`.github/` as canonical** (it already exists and is proven) and **generate `plugin/`** from it. The sync problem disappears — there's one place to edit, and `npm run build:plugin` regenerates the Claude Code side.

```
care_docs/
├── .claude-plugin/marketplace.json   ← catalog, source: "./plugin"
├── .github/                          ← CANONICAL (edit here)
├── plugin/                           ← GENERATED (commit it; do not edit)
│   ├── .claude-plugin/plugin.json
│   ├── agents/*.md
│   ├── skills/care-docs-generation/
│   └── recordings/
└── scripts/build-plugin.mjs
```

Users install with `/plugin marketplace add ohcnetwork/care_docs` → `/plugin install care-docs@ohcnetwork`. Docs content (`Clinical/…`) stays out of the plugin cache because the marketplace `source` points at `./plugin`.

## What the generator translates

| Concern | `.github/` (VS Code) | `plugin/` (Claude Code) |
|---|---|---|
| Model | `["Claude Sonnet 5 (copilot)"]` | `sonnet` / `opus` (inferred) |
| Tools | `read, search, edit, execute, agent, todo` | `Read`, `Glob`+`Grep`, `Write`+`Edit`, `Bash`, `Task`, `TodoWrite` |
| Filename | `care-docs-writer.agent.md` | `care-docs-writer.md` |
| Skill paths | `care_docs/.github/skills/…` | `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/…` |
| Repo paths | `~/ohc.network/care` | `$CARE_DIR` / `$CARE_FE_DIR` / `$CARE_DOCS_DIR` |

The script (~150 lines, no dependencies) is written and ready — manifest, agent frontmatter translation, skill copy with path rewriting, and the recordings harness bundled.

## Two things that need real decisions, not just codegen

1. **`agents:` allowlist has no Claude Code equivalent.** Your orchestrator (now *Ezhuthachan*) restricts itself to five named subagents. Claude Code selects subagents by description matching, so that constraint degrades to prose. Worth tightening the five descriptions so they don't over-trigger.

2. **Recording needs env vars, and this is the bulk of the remaining work.** [care.ts](../care_docs/recordings/support/care.ts) hardcodes `../care_fe` and `http://localhost:9000`; [codebase-navigation.md](../care_docs/.github/skills/care-docs-generation/references/codebase-navigation.md) and [flow-recording.md](../care_docs/.github/skills/care-docs-generation/references/flow-recording.md) hardcode `~/ohc.network/…`. These become `CARE_DIR`, `CARE_FE_DIR`, `CARE_DOCS_DIR`, `CARE_API_URL`, with a first-run setup skill that detects or asks. Node modules and Playwright browsers install into `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` — which the docs explicitly recommend for "dependencies that should survive plugin updates", so recording *can* ship fully working.

The recorder is instructed to do this, with `test.describe.serial` as the escape hatch for flows that genuinely can't be isolated, and `--workers=1` as a last resort it must report.
